t0.narrative: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is in its group stage (Jun 11 – Jul 19, current date Jun 21), with the expanded 48-team format — 16 groups of 3, top 2 advancing — reducing each team to just 2 group matches, eliminating margin for error and amplifying upset risk. Pre-tournament power rankings favor France, Argentina, England, Brazil, and Spain, but live group standings, match results, injuries, and form data are inaccessible at generation time, making any fixture-specific prediction unreliable below 0.40 confidence. A useful prediction requires knowing: which teams have already played, current group points and goal differential, injury status of key players, and match-specific incentives (must-win vs. draw-sufficient). Without these, I can only offer a structural framework — not a forecast.

sections.title: Tournament State (Jun 21, 2026)
sections.summary: The World Cup is underway, roughly 10 days into the group stage. The 48-team/16-group format is unprecedented.
bullets: 48 teams across 16 groups of 3 — each team plays 2 group matches
Top 2 from each group advance to 32-team knockout bracket
Group stage: Jun 11–27; Round of 32 begins Jun 28
Knockout bracket is fixed by group position (no re-draw)
Penalty shootouts for drawn group matches (new FIFA rule for 2026)
Host cities: 11 USA, 2 Canada, 3 Mexico — extreme travel distances

sections.title: Pre-Tournament Power Rankings
sections.summary: Based on Jan 2026 Elo ratings, squad market value, and recent major tournament performance.
bullets: Tier 1 (championship favorites): France, Argentina, England
Tier 2 (strong contenders): Brazil, Spain, Portugal, Germany
Tier 3 (dark horses): Netherlands, Uruguay, Italy, Croatia
Tier 4 (knockout threats): Morocco, Japan, Senegal, Colombia
Key player dependencies: Messi (ARG), Mbappe (FRA), Kane/Bellingham (ENG), Vinicius (BRA) — injury to any one shifts odds 15-25%

sections.title: Format-Induced Volatility
sections.summary: The 3-team group structure is the biggest structural uncertainty in tournament history.
bullets: 50% fewer group matches per team vs. 2022 (2 vs. 3) — no recovery from an opening loss
Penalty shootouts for tied group matches prevent deadlocked tables but add random variance
Risk of collusion in final group match when both teams can advance with a specific result
Teams playing 2nd group match last have information advantage over those who finish early
32/48 advance (66.7%) — high survival rate, but group position determines knockout path quality

sections.title: Host Nation Advantages
sections.summary: Historical host-nation premium is ~+0.45 goals per match. USA and Mexico have favorable draws.
bullets: USA: Pot 1 seeding, favorable group, home crowds in LA/Seattle
Mexico: Estadio Azteca altitude (2,240m) is a proven home advantage
Canada: Tougher group draw; Davies and David are the offensive engine
Host nations have reached knockout stage in 20 of last 22 World Cups

sections.title: What a Prediction Needs (Currently Missing)
sections.summary: A credible fixture-level forecast requires data that is blocked from retrieval at generation time.
bullets: Group standings: who has played, points, goal differential — the single most predictive variable
Match results so far: who has won, lost, drawn — reveals form and momentum
Injury reports: which key players are available or out — shifts match odds materially
Lineup and tactical trends: formations, pressing intensity, set-piece effectiveness
Weather forecasts for match venues: heat in Houston/Dallas/Monterrey, altitude in Mexico City
Betting market odds (implied probabilities): efficient aggregation of all above information

Teams play 2 group matches instead of 3; penalty shootouts for draws; 32-team knockout; FIFA Council confirmed format changes in 2024
